response: In AmazonHistoryPrice, OG-Narrator substantially improved the unaligned Phi-2 buyer: Phi-2’s deal rate rose from 13.64% to 88.08%, with SNP increasing from -1.58 to 2015.98 and share from -31.56% to 284.74%. The paper explicitly notes that this worked “even [for] a model that has not been aligned.” By contrast, in EAI, OpenChat-7b was reported to have notably high acceptance rates in both English and Russian, indicating a greater willingness to accept lower offers / cooperate than strongly RLHF-aligned Llama-2 models, which showed lower acceptance rates and a stricter threshold. So the AmazonHistoryPrice result is an intervention-driven boost in bargaining cooperation/performance for an unaligned model, whereas EAI reports an intrinsic model tendency of OpenChat-7b toward higher acceptance/cooperation compared with Llama-2.
judge_justification: The response correctly compares the two papers: it notes that OG-Narrator dramatically improves the unaligned Phi-2 model’s bargaining performance/deal rate in AmazonHistoryPrice, while EAI finds OpenChat-7b has a high propensity to accept offers/cooperate relative to strongly RLHF-aligned Llama-2. It captures the key synthesis that one result is an intervention-driven improvement for an unaligned model, whereas the other is an intrinsic tendency toward cooperation/acceptance in an uncensored model.
